task: Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Open the door, then pick up the box in the other room.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Existence(target_picked_up) and Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) are correct. But the soft Absence(key_lost) does not capture “Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed”: it penalizes key_lost even if the key was not dropped while the door was closed, and omits that stated condition. Use a soft Precedence(door_open, key_lost) to prohibit key_lost before the door opens.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The soft Precedence(door_open, key_lost) does not capture “Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.” That task phrase bans dropping the key while the door is closed, regardless of whether it was opened earlier; key_lost is only a one-step event when the key is dropped before the door opens, so it misses later drops after the door is closed again. Use a soft Absence(key_lost) only if key_lost represents every such drop; with the supplied event definition, it does not, so the candidate cannot express this ban using key_lost. The hard Existence(target_picked_up) and Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) correctly require picking up the box after opening the door.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: The soft Absence(key_lost) captures “Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.” The hard Existence(target_picked_up) requires picking up the box, and hard Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) captures opening the door first.

texts: Prefer not to lose the key while the door is closed.
Pick up the box after opening the door.
The door must be open before the box is picked up.
